title: Archipel extensions to ACP v2 (draft)
description: Root type used only to generate `schema/archipel.schema.json`.

ArchipelMeta.description: Added by the daemon under `_meta.archipel` on every `session/update` it sends.

seq.description: Position of this update in the session's log. Starts at 1 and has no gaps.

rootSessionId.description:
The session whose log this is, when the message belongs to a subagent's child session.
Absent when it equals the message's own `sessionId`.

UpdateOrigin.description: Under `_meta.archipel` inside an update body that did not come from the agent.

addon.description: The id of the addon, when `origin` is `addon`.

agentId.description: The agent to create the session with. Absent for the daemon's first agent.

AgentInfo.description: One agent the daemon can start.

agentId.description: Stable id used in other calls, such as `claude` or `pi`.

version.description: Version of the adapter, when known.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation when the agent is not ready.

capabilities.description:
What the agent said it can do in its `initialize` answer, once it has been started.
`session.title`, `session.delete` and `session.options` say whether a session can be
renamed, deleted, and its settings read before it exists. Absent until the agent has
started: `_archipel/sessions/list` with its id starts it.

oneOf.description:
The daemon has not started it yet, so nothing is known about it. The first request
that needs the agent starts it; `_archipel/sessions/list` with its id is one.
Being started: its process runs and has not answered `initialize` yet.
Installed, but the user has to log in with the harness itself.
Its program was not found when the daemon tried to start it. `detail` names it.
It could not be started, or stopped with an error. `detail` says why.

cwd.description: Only sessions in this working directory.

loggedOnly.description: Leave out sessions that only the harness knows. This never starts an adapter.

limit.description: At most this many sessions, newest first. Absent for all of them.

cursor.description:
`nextCursor` of a previous response, to get the sessions after that page. A session
that changes between two pages moves to the front, where `_archipel/sessions/updated`
has already reported it.

nextCursor.description: Present when `limit` left sessions out: pass it as `cursor` for the next page.

live.description: True when an adapter process currently holds the session.

logged.description:
True when the session is in the daemon's log. False for a session only the harness
knows, for example one started in the harness's own UI: attaching to it, or sending it
anything, makes the daemon load its history from the harness first.

openElsewhere.description:
True when another process of the harness has the session open right now, for example
the harness's own terminal UI. The daemon then refuses to act on the session; it can
still be read, and `session/fork` makes a copy to continue with.

state.description: The last ACP `state_update` state, such as `idle` or `running`, when known.

headSeq.description: Sequence number of the newest update in the log.

updatedAt.description: RFC 3339 time of the newest update.

AttachSessionRequest.description:
`_archipel/session/attach` request: start receiving a session's updates.

The response comes first, then the catch-up, then live messages.

afterSeq.description: The last sequence number the client has applied. Absent to get the whole session.

catchUp.description: How the client is brought up to date.

headSeq.description: Sequence number of the newest update at the time of the response.

openElsewhere.description:
Another process of the harness has the session open. It can be read, but the daemon
refuses to act on it; `session/fork` makes a copy to continue with.

oneOf.description: The updates after `afterSeq` follow. The client keeps its state.

A condensed replay of the whole session follows, ending with `replay_complete`.
The client discards its state for this session first.

OpenElsewhere.description: The `data` of an [`ERROR_OPEN_ELSEWHERE`] error: who has the session open.

status.description: What that process says it is doing, such as `busy` or `idle`.

client.description: How that process was started, such as `cli`.

DetachSessionRequest.description: `_archipel/session/detach` request: stop receiving updates. The session keeps running.

RequestResolvedNotification.description: `_archipel/request/resolved`: a pending approval or question was answered, possibly by another client.

requestId.description: The id of the request. It is the JSON-RPC id the daemon sent the request with.

method.description: The method of the request, such as `session/request_permission`.

params.description: The params of the request. Present in a replay, where the request itself is not sent.

outcome.description: The answer that was given, in the shape of the method's response.

resolvedBy.description: A label for the client that answered, when known.

SessionsUpdatedNotification.description: `_archipel/sessions/updated`: a session appeared or its summary changed. Sent to every app.

SessionsRemovedNotification.description:
`_archipel/sessions/removed`: a session was deleted at its harness through the daemon, which
dropped its log too. Sent to every app.

SessionErrorNotification.description:
`_archipel/session/error`: something went wrong in a session outside any request, so there
is no response to carry the error. `code` and `message` mean what they mean in a JSON-RPC
error. Sent to the attached apps and not stored.

With [`ERROR_STORAGE`]: updates of the session are being lost, because the log cannot be
written. It is sent once, when the first write fails, not for every lost update. What is
lost is not sent to any app, so no app holds more than the log does.

Scope.description: What a connected app may do. Each level includes the ones before it.

oneOf.description: Also create sessions, prompt, cancel, answer, change settings.
Also act as an extension: register a namespace, add items to sessions, serve methods.
Also delete sessions and manage the daemon.

RegisterExtensionRequest.description:
`_archipel/extension/register` request: this connection is the extension `namespace`.

From then on it may add updates whose kind starts with `x.<namespace>.` to sessions, and
the daemon passes it every request whose method starts with `_x/<namespace>/`.

AppendRequest.description:
`_archipel/session/append` request: add an update of the extension's own kind to a session.
It is numbered, stored, replayed and sent to every attached app like any other update.

update.description: The update body. Its `sessionUpdate` must start with `x.<namespace>.`.

state.description:
How the update changes what clients hold. Without it the update is kept as an event
that clients do not place among the items.

ItemRule.description:
How an extension's update changes client state: an ACP state rule whose target is the
update's own kind. The daemon stores it in the update under `_meta.archipel.state`, so every
client can apply it without knowing the extension.

id.description: Dotted path of the item's id in the update, such as `checkpointId`.

field.description: The field of the item that is changed. Absent means the whole item.

value.description: Dotted path of the new data in the update. Absent means the whole update.

seq.description: The sequence number the update got.
